skill.name: context7-efficient
skill.description: Fetches Context7 library documentation through shell scripts, then filters the response into concise code examples, API signatures, and notes.
skill.summary: Fetch Context7 documentation with token-efficient shell filtering.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate documentation-fetching intent, and many static hits are markdown backticks or Context7 reference text. Real risks remain from shell execution, shell=True stdio handling, unpinned npx package execution, unescaped JSON parameter construction, and predictable /tmp PID files. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The MCP client executes --stdio command strings with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with an argument array, parse commands with shlex only when needed, and allowlist the Context7 MCP command used by this skill.

remediation.issue: Scripts execute an unpinned npx package for Context7 MCP.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @upstash/context7-mcp to a reviewed version or ship a lockfile-backed wrapper, and document the outbound network behavior.

remediation.issue: JSON request bodies are assembled with shell interpolation.
remediation.suggestion: Build MCP parameters with Python json.dumps or jq, validate page and mode values, and escape library and topic strings structurally.

remediation.issue: Server lifecycle scripts trust predictable PID files in /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Store PID files in a user-owned runtime directory, validate the port as a number, check process ownership, and avoid broad pkill patterns.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Stdio Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The MCP client exposes a --stdio option and passes that command string to subprocess.Popen with shell=True. This turns the helper into a general shell execution wrapper if untrusted input controls the stdio command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is accepted from a CLI argument and executed through shell=True. The code path is direct and does not apply an allowlist or argument array.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned NPM MCP Server Execution
semantic_findings.description: The scripts run npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp without a pinned package version. This can execute changed remote package code during documentation fetches or server startup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple scripts invoke the same unversioned npx package. The behavior is intentional but creates a clear supply-chain execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped JSON Parameter Construction
semantic_findings.description: Shell heredocs and inline strings interpolate library, topic, mode, and page values into JSON without json.dumps or another structured encoder. Malformed input can alter or break MCP parameters.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The variables are quoted for the shell, so direct command injection is unlikely. They are still inserted into JSON syntax without escaping or type validation.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temporary PID File Controls Process Termination
semantic_findings.description: The server control scripts use predictable /tmp PID files and then trust those files when checking or killing processes. Stale or locally modified files can affect which process is targeted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The PID file path is deterministic and stored under /tmp, and stop-server.sh sends normal and forced kill signals based on that state. The impact depends on local filesystem access and execution privileges.

content.value_statement: Library documentation often returns too much text for focused coding tasks. This skill fetches Context7 documentation and filters it into concise examples, signatures, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Resolves library names to Context7-compatible library IDs.
Fetches documentation by library ID, topic, mode, and page.
Filters raw documentation into code examples, API signatures, and notes.
Supports code-focused and concept-focused documentation modes.
Provides helper scripts to start and stop a local Context7 MCP server.
limitations: Requires Bash, Python 3, npx, and network access to Context7 tooling.
Runs an external npm MCP package through shell commands.
Filtering can omit useful context from long documentation pages.
It does not verify returned documentation against project-specific versions.

faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it use shell scripts?
faq.answer: The scripts keep large raw documentation responses outside the assistant context and return filtered text.

faq.question: Does it validate documentation versions?
faq.answer: No. It requests Context7 documentation but does not verify version alignment with a local project.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the shell scripts, npx package execution, network behavior, and MCP client command handling.
